metadata.title: Round 2 SME Review Packet
metadata.subtitle: Compensation · Benefits · Global Mobility · Total Rewards Advisory
metadata.time_required: About 75 minutes for this focus group

how_this_works.what_we_did: We combined your Round 1 edits, comment by comment, into one proposed version of each competency. Where several specializations edited the same competency we kept as many requested changes as possible, merged the named methods and standards, and where edits conflicted we weighted the owner's version. Changes that were clear and agreed have already been applied; they appear in Part A. Where reviewers saw the work differently, or where a change shifts who owns it, we drafted a recommendation rather than deciding for you; those appear in Part B.
how_this_works.what_we_need: For Part A, read each applied change and confirm it fits your specialization or note a correction. For Part B, review the recommendation and bring your view to the focus group. Nothing in Part B is final until the group decides.
how_this_works.where_feedback_went: Every Round 1 comment is accounted for in the appendix disposition. If you do not see one of your edits in the wording, the disposition states how it was used or why it was adjusted.
how_this_works.status_intro: Every competency below carries a status label so you can see, at a glance, what is already settled and what still needs the group. Items are grouped into two parts: Part A holds changes we have already applied (read and confirm); Part B holds the items for live discussion (decisions and proposals).

ground_rules.text: Decide who designs, advises, or administers, and at what level, before debating wording.
Where Clinton Shoap (SVP, Total Rewards) and another reviewer proposed conflicting edits to the same shared competency, the SVP wording governs and is shown as the owner version.
Owners and dates recorded at sign-off feed the decision registry; the sub-family owner is John.

start_here.heading: Start here: agree the design-versus-facilitation convention
start_here.intro: Total Rewards owns the design and governance of pay, benefits, and mobility programs, while advisors and administrators facilitate, apply, and use those programs. Place each role on the ladder rather than rewriting a shared competency for each one.

rows: Net user or facilitator
1 to 2
Applies, advises on, or facilitates programs others design; not accountable for building them
Accountable designer
Designs and deploys programs and owns the decisions made from them
Owner or standard-setter
Defines the strategy, governance, and standards others follow

quote.label: A quote that sets the line (Total Rewards Advisory).
quote.text: This is written more aligned to a Domain. TRA plays a role in this but often does not own the frameworks used. We are net users of info, not developers of it typically.

start_here.decide: Adopt this convention for today, then apply it to the shared competencies below.

coverage.legend: D designs and owns (Levels 3 to 4) · C carries with the specialization lens · F facilitates · U uses and applies (Levels 1 to 2) · A advises (apply-and-advise) · Aw awareness (Levels 1 to 2) · S shared employment-practice anchor · L2 limited (Level 2) · def deferred.
coverage.note: Benefits Program Strategy & Management is also administered by Benefits Administration (Leave & Benefits Administration) in HR Operations at Levels 1 to 2. Workforce Planning & Capability Strategy was removed from the Compensation set and is replaced for Total Rewards Advisory by Organization Design & Operating Models (Decisions 2 and 5). Labor Relations & Bargaining is deferred from the Total Rewards Advisory set under AS-7 (set-size ceiling of eight); def means deferred.

ratings_legend.heading: How to read the Round 1 ratings
rows: Essential
Jobs in this specialization cannot perform core work without this capability. Absence equals role failure.
Very important
Jobs perform noticeably better with strong capability. Weak capability creates measurable friction and rework.
Important
Useful and expected, but not a differentiator. Other competencies carry more weight day to day.
Limited
Occasionally relevant. Not a reliable predictor of performance for this specialization.
Low
Rarely relevant. Borderline for inclusion in this specialization.

part_b.intro: Each item below was seen differently by reviewers or shifts who owns the work. A recommendation is drafted for the group. Full indicator tables for every competency in play are in the appendix.

items.title: Benefits Program Strategy & Management: design and governance, the rename, and operational scope
items.owners_line: Benefits (owner), Global Mobility, Total Rewards Advisory   |   15 min

rows: Change this to Benefits Program Strategy, Design and Governance and move more operational components to HR Service Delivery Excellence or HR Compliance & Workforce Risk. (361 insertions, 170 deletions synthesized.)
Relevant and essential for Global Mobility, but the current framing is too benefits-oriented. Make the mobility dimension more explicit by reflecting international assignment activity.
Current wording is very design and programmatic; TRA plays more of a facilitation role. Need to re-assess Level alignment once we see the updated definition.

items.recommendation: Keep this as the shared benefits-and-mobility program competency. The v5 wording already merges the well-being and governance additions and the mobility dimension (see appendix). Resolve the rename to Benefits Program Strategy, Design and Governance, and decide which operational components move to HR Service Delivery Excellence and HR Compliance. Apply the convention across the roles that touch it: Benefits owns design and governance at Levels 3 to 4; Global Mobility carries it with the mobility lens; Total Rewards Advisory facilitates at apply-and-advise levels; and Benefits Administration (HR Operations) administers at Levels 1 to 2. Because the competency is shared with Benefits Administration, the wording must hold a middle ground that reads for both design and administration.

decide.text: Adopt the rename? Which operational components move out, and to which competency? Confirm the design-versus-facilitation levels per role?

rows: Reauthored all four levels (data-maintenance facilitation, educate and train managers, stakeholder adoption, influence senior stakeholders, governance). Also: remove HR Service Delivery Excellence and Workforce Planning & Capability Strategy from the competencies used for this specialization.
Relevant for Global Mobility, but current wording is too broad and Compensation-centered. Tailor toward international assignment compensation.
TRA plays a role but often does not own the frameworks used. Can we broaden language to design and deployment?

items.recommendation: Adopt Clinton Shoap's reauthored wording as the authoritative owner version. Apply his set-membership change: remove HR Service Delivery Excellence and Workforce Planning & Capability Strategy from the Compensation specialization. The Compensation packet still lists Workforce Planning as an open decision tied to the enterprise Workforce Planning versus Talent Demand Planning question; the SVP removal resolves it for Compensation, and Talent Demand Planning is the Talent Acquisition demand-side replacement, not a Compensation competency. Honor the contributor views through level, not by overwriting the owner: Global Mobility carries Compensation with the international-assignment-compensation lens; Total Rewards Advisory sits at apply-and-advise levels, which accommodates the design-and-deployment framing without changing ownership.

decide.text: Adopt the SVP reauthored wording as authoritative, remove the two competencies from the Compensation set, and confirm the contributor levels?

items.title: Workforce Analytics & HR Insights: what each role does with data, and the boundary
items.owners_line: Compensation, Benefits, Total Rewards Advisory   |   10 min

note.text: Importance is settled and high; an earlier weakest label was a corrected data error. The Benefits and Compensation packets both route this as a live decision because reviewers saw the role of data differently. This is about what each role does with data and the levels, not whether it belongs.

rows: Rated a user-level competency (Limited). Compensation applies and interprets reward data; it does not build the analytics.
Apply a benefits data-analytics and reporting lens: plan utilization, financial forecasting, vendor performance, and cost modeling.
We are net users of info, not developers of it typically. Defer the build-level description to roles closer to the analytics work.

items.recommendation: Keep Workforce Analytics for Total Rewards at applied, use-not-own levels. Place Compensation, Benefits, and Total Rewards Advisory at Levels 1 to 2 with a rewards-and-benefits reporting lens (utilization, cost modeling, vendor performance, financial forecasting); they interpret and act on analytics rather than building tools. Add one boundary sentence so this does not duplicate the Common Technology & Data Acumen competency: this is the rewards-data application of analytics to Total Rewards decisions, not general data literacy.

decide.text: Confirm the use-not-own levels per role and the boundary sentence against the Common Technology & Data Acumen competency?

note.text: Before (as first drafted from Round 1): add Performance Management Program Design, Talent Review & Succession Management, and Labor Relations & Bargaining (three additions), then run a set-size check. After (this version): add Performance Management and Talent Review, swap Workforce Planning for Organization Design (net-neutral to set size), and defer Labor Relations & Bargaining. Rationale: adding all three would breach the AS-7 hard ceiling of eight competencies for the Total Rewards Advisory set, so net additions are capped at two. Source: AS-7 and tcb_as7_validator_v3_7. Owner: Chris Honts. Date: 2026-06-22. Revisit Labor Relations & Bargaining only if a competency is retired to make room.

rows: Performance Management Program Design and Talent Review & Succession Management should be considered given the considerable overlap between performance and pay.

Organization Design & Operating Models may be a better fit than Workforce Planning & Capability Strategy. We need something tied to job architecture. This competency would be an input to broader org work.
Labor Relations & Bargaining at Level 2 (limited). Workforce Planning is not TRA core work.

items.recommendation: For the Total Rewards Advisory set, add Performance Management Program Design and Talent Review & Succession Management at advisory (apply-and-advise) levels. Replace Workforce Planning & Capability Strategy with Organization Design & Operating Models as the job-architecture anchor (a net-neutral swap). Defer Labor Relations & Bargaining to keep the set within the AS-7 ceiling of eight; revisit it only if a competency is retired. With the two additions and the swap, the final set stays within range.

decide.text: Confirm the two additions (Performance Management and Talent Review), the Workforce Planning to Organization Design swap, and the deferral of Labor Relations & Bargaining per AS-7?

rows: Shared competencies span Total Rewards and HR Operations

appendix.intro: Current indicators for the competencies in play, with accepted Round 1 edits applied. Read these as reminders before the session. The session decides ownership and level, not the wording. Every Round 1 comment is accounted for in Appendix A.

indicators.text: Identifies workforce segments, capability terms, and demand assumptions from planning templates and job data.
Records headcount, skills, role, and vacancy information in workforce planning files.
Follows data-quality checks for workforce planning inputs, capability inventories, and scenario assumptions.
Builds workforce snapshots using job architecture data, skills taxonomy entries, role inventories, and demand inputs.
Conducts gap analyses comparing workforce supply, hiring plans, capability needs, and attrition patterns.
Maintains scenario files, action trackers, and planning dashboards for assigned workforce segments.
Designs workforce plans using competency frameworks, Cargill capability model inputs, demand forecasts, and business scenarios.
Evaluates build-buy-borrow scenarios through cost, risk, timeline, and capability impact analyses.
Leads workforce planning reviews that translate capability gaps into talent, hiring, and development actions.
Establishes enterprise workforce planning standards for capability taxonomies, forecasting methods, and scenario governance.
Approves strategic workforce planning models for critical capabilities, transformation portfolios, and long-range demand.
Develops advanced workforce-planning diagnostics that translate capability risk into portfolio, build-buy-borrow, and development choices.
